text: 🇲🇽✊ "The first thing we did was write women's rights into the Constitution — they weren't fully established there." "The first thing we did was take women's rights to the Constitution, where they were not fully established." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the foundation of the feminicide law The constitutional reform on women's rights is the base for the new law: unified definition, 50–70 years, imprescriptible, zero impunity.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico ranks 12th in the 2026 World Happiness Report — first in Latin America, and the most populous nation in the top 12. "People are content — though some aren't." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the World Happiness Report Gallup places Mexico 12th of all nations, 1st in Latin America, with 133M+ people — the largest population in the top tier. INEGI's life-satisfaction score rose from 8.45 (2021) to 8.62 (2025).

🔥🇲🇽 A former Pemex director — a longtime ally — was just detained on domestic violence charges. Sheinbaum didn't flinch. "Víctor's own arrest shows that regardless of friendship or position, the law has to be enforced… we will never protect anyone who breaks the law, and even less if there is violence against women." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the detention of Víctor Rodríguez Padilla No exception for closeness or rank — the same day she sent the feminicide law to Congress.

🇲🇽⚖️ Feminicide would become imprescriptible — no statute of limitations, no amnesty, no reduced sentences, ever. "This General Law guarantees that all of it can be reduced to the maximum, and that we truly have zero impunity for feminicides." — Claudia Sheinbaum, presenting the law The crime, its punishment and reparations would never expire. Prosecutors would be bound to investigate "with reinforced due diligence" under specialized gender-perspective protocols.

🇲🇽⚖️ Mexico's first woman president sends Congress a General Law on Feminicide — 50 to 70 years, uniform across all 32 states. "As the first woman President, I took on the responsibility of protecting women from violence. The worst crime of violence against women, the worst form of discrimination and indignity, is death — feminicide." — Claudia Sheinbaum, signing the initiative The bill unifies the definition of feminicide nationwide with 19 aggravating factors. Congress takes it up in September.

🇲🇽🌎 "Results are always better when we cooperate than when someone acts unilaterally — even violating sovereignty." "Results are always better when we cooperate than when someone acts unilaterally, even violating sovereignty." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the US capture of "El Mayo" Zambada Washington's unilateral operation split the Sinaloa Cartel and set off a wave of violence. She said she can raise it directly with Trump.

🚨🇲🇽 The DEA director claimed a "deadly connection" between Mexico's government and cartels. Sheinbaum's answer was flat. "We categorically deny the DEA director's assertion. The DEA has plenty to do in its own country and within its own organization. The largest drug market in the world is in the United States. Mexico is to be respected." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on DEA director Terry Cole's accusation Homicides are down 48% under her government — a state tied to cartels could not cut crime. She noted former DEA official Nicholas Palmeri was removed over improper ties to cartel lawyers.

🇲🇽🌎 TRUMP TAXED THEM. THEY SENT MORE ANYWAY.

Mexican remittances hit $5.611 billion in May — up 3.8% year-on-year and a fourth straight month of growth — even after Trump signed a decree forcing banks to police migrant transfers, per Banxico. The money that keeps millions of families and half the towns of Michoacán and Oaxaca running doesn't ask Washington's permission to cross the river.

🚨🇲🇽 EVEN THE IACHR IS DEMANDING ANSWERS FOR MIGRANTS KILLED BY ICE

The Inter-American Commission on Human Rights formally demanded independent, impartial investigations into migrants killed in ICE operations — among them Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a Mexican, shot dead in Houston. "The use of force must adhere strictly to international standards," the CIDH said. Mexico has already filed criminal complaints for its dead. Washington still calls this "enforcement."

🔥🇲🇽 THE REAL NARCO-GOVERNMENTS FLEW A PARTY LOGO: PAN

Morena's Ariadna Montiel laid out the record: El Chapo walked out of Puente Grande in 2001 under Fox and stayed free through all six years of Calderón — "for more than 12 years this crime boss was never captured." Calderón's own party ran one of Chapo's lovers for office, and his security chief Genaro García Luna now sits in a US federal prison, convicted of trafficking. Remember who lectures Mexico about "cartel links."
